steps.do: Check that the html element carries a lang attribute.
Check that the Arabic list page sets dir to rtl exactly once.
Run axe against the served Arabic list page using WCAG 2A rules.

K-019502.example: The grep prints the html tag with lang="ar" dir="rtl" and the count prints 1. The axe run should report 0 violations, so html-has-lang and valid-lang both pass.
K-019502.check: grep prints the html tag with lang="ar" and dir="rtl", the count prints 1, and axe prints 0 violations.
traps: Small models often put dir on the ul instead of the html root, which misses page-level direction.
lang sets the language but dir is a separate attribute and both are needed.
Re-run axe after every locale change, not only once.

steps.do: Search the list stylesheet for physical left and right properties.
Replace each physical property with its logical equivalent such as margin-inline-start.
Run the Playwright RTL test that checks bullet and padding position on the Arabic list.

K-019503.example: The grep first printed padding-left: 16px on line 22 of styles/list.css, which is changed to padding-inline-start: 1rem. After the change, the grep prints nothing and the Playwright run prints 1 passed.
K-019503.check: The grep prints no lines after the fix, and Playwright reports 1 passed with 0 failed.
traps: Small models often change only the value and keep the physical property name, which does not flip in RTL.
Logical properties need the exact names such as padding-inline-start, not a guessed variant.
Check the grep output again after editing because one missed line breaks the mirror.

steps.do: Print the German conjunction output for three items with Node.
Print the English conjunction output for the same three items to compare.
Confirm app.js builds the joined text with ListFormat and not a hand-written join.

K-019504.example: The German run prints Äpfel, Birnen und Trauben and the English run prints apples, pears, and grapes. The grep should show the line in app.js that calls new Intl.ListFormat with the current document language.
K-019504.check: Node prints the German string with und before the last item, and grep prints at least one line containing ListFormat.
traps: Small models often hand-join with a comma and the word and, which fails for German and Arabic.
The conjunction word and the Oxford comma differ by locale, so only ListFormat gets them right.
Pass the page locale to ListFormat, not a hard-coded 'en'.

steps.do: Run the full list locale Playwright suite with the line reporter.
Confirm the list item minimum block size is 44px for touch targets.
Run Lighthouse accessibility on the Arabic list page in headless Chrome.

K-019505.example: Playwright prints 6 passed, grep prints the min-block-size line with 44px, and Lighthouse prints an accessibility score of 0.97. The score is above the 0.95 gate, so the list passes.
K-019505.check: Playwright reports 0 failed, grep finds the 44px line, and Lighthouse accessibility score is 0.95 or higher.
traps: Small models often read a passing Playwright run as proof of accessibility, but Lighthouse measures contrast and labels separately.
A missing min-block-size line means touch targets may be under 44px even if tests pass.
Lighthouse needs the page served on a running server, not a file path.

steps.do: Count all hreflang tags in the English list page. Expect the number 4: en, ar, de, and x-default.
Count the x-default link. Expect the number 1.
Request the English alternate and print its HTTP status code. Expect 200.
Request the German alternate and print its HTTP status code. Expect 200.
Request the Arabic alternate and print its HTTP status code. Expect 200.
Request the German alternate and print its total response time in seconds. Expect a number under 0.200.
Request the Arabic alternate and print its total response time in seconds. Expect a number under 0.200.

K-019506.example: The count prints 4 for en, ar, de, and x-default. The x-default count prints 1. The English, German, and Arabic requests print 200. The German response prints 0.118 and the Arabic response prints 0.142, both under 0.200 seconds.
K-019506.check: The hreflang count prints 4, the x-default count prints 1, each of the three alternates returns 200, and each response time is under 0.200 seconds.
traps: Small models often add hreflang only to the English page, but each page needs links to all alternates including itself.
A 404 alternate breaks the whole set, so check every URL returns 200.
grep -c counts lines and reports 1 on minified HTML, so use the Python count.
Do not count the x-default link as a locale; it is a separate tag.

steps.do: Search the token file for every tabs variable.
Confirm the tab font size token is set to 1rem.
Confirm the tab label font weight token is defined once.

K-019507.example: The file src/lib/styles/tokens.css should contain --tabs-font-size: 1rem and --tabs-font-weight: 500 on their own lines. The count command should print 1 for the weight token.
K-019507.check: The first search prints at least 4 matching lines, the second prints exactly one line ending in 1rem, and the third prints 1; any miss means the tokens are not wired up.
traps: Small models often invent token names instead of grepping the real file first. Use only names the search returns.
Setting the font size in px breaks user zoom. The token must be 1rem so it follows the root font size.

steps.do: Install the axe integration for Playwright as a dev dependency.
Add a test that runs AxeBuilder with include set to the toast region selector [role=status] and withTags set to wcag2aa.
Run the contrast test on the mobile-375 project.

K-019508.example: The success toast uses #1f6f3a text on #e8f5ec background, which measures about 5.9:1. The axe run reports zero color-contrast violations for the toast region.
K-019508.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and the test asserts results.violations has length 0 for rule color-contrast.
traps: Small models often run axe on the whole page, which hides toast-specific failures behind unrelated ones. Scope include to the toast region.
Axe only finds the toast if it is open during the scan. Trigger the toast in the test before calling analyze().

steps.do: Open the global stylesheet to see existing custom properties.
Add a :root block that sets --select-font-family to system-ui, sans-serif, --select-font-size to 1rem, --select-line-height to 1.5, --select-font-weight to 400 and --select-letter-spacing to 0.01em.
Count the lines that define select tokens to confirm all five are present.
Run the Svelte type check to confirm nothing else broke.

K-019509.example: The :root block sets --select-font-size to 1rem, which is 16px at the default browser size. The grep prints 5 because five lines contain select-.
K-019509.check: grep prints 5 and svelte-check ends with 0 errors.
traps: Small models often write 16px instead of 1rem, which ignores user font scaling.
They also put the tokens inside the component instead of :root, so other components cannot share them.

steps.do: Create the component file at src/lib/Select.svelte.
Declare props with $props and mark value with $bindable so the parent can two-way bind it.
Render a label with a for attribute matching id, then a native select with an {#each} block over options.
In a scoped style block, set font-family, font-size and line-height to the var(--select-...) tokens.
Build the project to confirm the component compiles.

K-019510.example: A parent writes bind:value={color} on Select with options set to colors and id set to color. The select reads font-size from var(--select-font-size), so it renders at 1rem.
K-019510.check: npm run build exits with code 0 and prints a built in line.
traps: Small models often use export let, which is Svelte 4 syntax, instead of $props.
They also forget $bindable, so bind:value fails silently.

steps.do: Open the component to find the scoped style block.
Change each token reference to the form var(--select-font-size, 1rem) with the fallback after the comma.
List every line that uses var to confirm each reference has a fallback.
Run Prettier in check mode on the component.

K-019511.example: font-size: var(--select-font-size, 1rem) still gives 16px if the token is missing. The rg output lists 4 lines with var, and each one has a comma before the fallback.
K-019511.check: prettier prints All matched files use Prettier code style! and every var reference has a comma.
traps: Small models put the fallback before the comma or use px only.
They also add fallbacks to the :root definitions themselves, which hides missing tokens.

steps.do: Find the existing light mode token block in app.css.
Add a block with the selector [data-theme='dark'] that overrides --select-fg to #f2f2f2, --select-bg to #1a1a1a and --select-border to #444444.
Set color-scheme to dark inside that block so native dropdown menus match the theme.
Confirm the dark selector appears exactly once in the stylesheet.
Run the Svelte type check.

K-019512.example: [data-theme='dark'] sets the text to #f2f2f2 on a #1a1a1a background, a contrast of about 15.6:1. The grep prints one line containing the dark selector.
K-019512.check: grep prints one matching line and the text and background pair has a contrast of at least 4.5:1.
traps: Small models override only the text color and leave the native dropdown in light colors.
They also pick hex values without checking contrast, so text can fall below 4.5:1.

steps.do: Add --select-min-height set to 2.75rem in the :root block of app.css, which equals 44px at the default root size.
Apply min-height set to var(--select-min-height) and padding-inline set to 0.75rem in the scoped style block.
Create an end to end spec file for the select.
Write the spec to read the select bounding box height and expect at least 44.
Run the Playwright spec for the select.

K-019513.example: The select renders 44px tall at the default 16px root size, which meets the target. The spec reads boundingBox().height and expects a value of 44 or more.
K-019513.check: Playwright reports 1 passed and the measured height is 44 or more.
traps: Small models write 44 without a unit, which is invalid CSS.
They also set padding but not min-height, so short labels make the select shorter than 44px.

steps.do: Search the component for pixel font sizes.
Replace each match with var(--select-font-size) in the scoped style block.
Run the same search again to confirm it returns no matches.
Lint the component with the project ESLint config.

K-019514.example: The first grep prints a line such as font-size: 14px, which is the forbidden value. After the fix the second grep prints nothing and eslint exits with code 0.
K-019514.check: The second grep prints nothing and eslint exits with code 0 and no output.
traps: Small models treat grep exit code 1 as an error, but for no matches it means success.
They also fix only the first match and miss a second px line.

steps.do: Run svelte-check against the project tsconfig.
Confirm the Tabs props type is exported from the types file.
Confirm Tabs.svelte imports and uses TabsProps.

K-019515.example: Tabs.svelte declares its props with let { tabs, active = 0 }: TabsProps = $props(); and TabsProps lives in src/lib/types.ts. svelte-check should report no errors for that file.
K-019515.check: The svelte-check output ends with a line reading svelte-check found 0 errors and 0 warnings, the first grep prints one line with export type TabsProps, and the second grep prints at least one line with TabsProps in Tabs.svelte.
traps: Svelte 4 syntax like export let and on:click does not match Svelte 5 runes; use $props() and onclick.
A zero-error run on an unchanged file does not prove the styles work. Run the browser tests as well.

steps.do: Search Tabs.svelte for hex color literals.
Search Tabs.svelte for pixel font sizes.
Confirm the component reads color from var() tokens.
Run stylelint with the project config on Tabs.svelte to flag raw colors and px font sizes.

K-019516.example: A line like color: #1d4ed8; in Tabs.svelte fails the first search. The correct form is color: var(--tabs-tab-color); which the count search picks up.
K-019516.check: The first two searches print no lines and exit with code 1, the third prints a count of at least 3, and stylelint reports 0 problems; any printed hex value or px size means the card failed.
traps: Small models sometimes replace hex with rgb() and think the check passed. The search must find no color literals of any kind.
Values inside a <style> block still count. Do not exempt them from the search.

steps.do: Run the typography spec that reads computed styles on each tab label.
Confirm the spec file asserts a 16px computed font size.
List the tests in the typography spec to confirm both are present.

K-019517.example: The spec opens /tabs-demo, reads getComputedStyle(tab).fontSize for each button role="tab", and expects 16px with a line-height of at least 24px. The run reports two passed tests.
K-019517.check: Playwright prints 2 passed and 0 failed, the grep prints the line containing 16px, and the --list output shows 2 tests; a font size of 14px or a line height under 24px means the typography is wrong.
traps: Small models often assert the CSS source text instead of the computed value in the browser. Read the rendered style with getComputedStyle.
Root font size can be changed in the test page, so 1rem is not always 16px. Check the actual root value too.

steps.do: Run the accessibility spec that scans the tabs page with axe.
Confirm the spec scans for the color-contrast rule.
Confirm the spec checks the active and disabled tab states.

K-019518.example: Dark text #1f2937 on a white tab background is 14.7:1 and passes. A gray label #9ca3af on white is about 2.5:1 and fails the 4.5:1 rule that axe reports.
K-019518.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, the axe report lists 0 color-contrast violations for the Tabs region, and the grep for aria-selected or disabled prints at least 2 lines; any violation with a ratio below 4.5:1 means the card failed.
traps: Small models often check only the default tab and skip the active and disabled states. Scan each state.
Large text needs only 3:1, but tab labels are normal text, so they need 4.5:1.

steps.do: Run the target-size spec that measures each tab button with boundingBox.
Lint Tabs.svelte to confirm no rule flags the markup or styles.
Confirm the 44px minimum height token is set in Tabs.svelte.
Confirm the visible focus ring token is defined in Tabs.svelte.

K-019519.example: The spec reads each button role="tab" with boundingBox() and expects height of at least 44px and width of at least 44px. The token --tabs-tab-min-height: 44px sets the minimum.
K-019519.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, eslint prints no problems, the grep for --tabs-tab-min-height: 44px prints one line, and the grep for --tabs-focus-ring prints at least one line; any tab whose height is below 44px means the card failed.
traps: Small models often test only the visual size and not the clickable box. Measure the element's bounding box.
A focus outline removed with outline: none fails keyboard users. Keep a visible focus ring token in the stylesheet.

steps.do: In tests/toast.responsive.spec.ts, call page.setViewportSize with width 320 and height 568 before triggering a toast.
Run the spec on the mobile-320 project.
In the spec, assert document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals 320 after the toast mounts.

K-019520.example: Trigger a success toast from App.tsx at 320px wide. The spec asserts scrollWidth is 320, not 340, so the toast does not push the page sideways.
K-019520.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and no line says 'Expected 320 Received 340'.
traps: Small models often test only at 1280px and assume mobile works. Always set the 320px viewport explicitly in the spec.
A fixed min-width such as 360px on the toast causes overflow. Use width: min(100% - 2rem, 24rem) instead.

steps.do: In tests/touch-target.spec.ts, add a test named touch target that gets the close button with getByRole('button', { name: 'Dismiss' }) and reads boundingBox().
Run only the test named touch target on the mobile-375 project.
In the same spec, assert box.width and box.height are each at least 44 CSS pixels.

K-019521.example: The close button is a 24px icon by default. After setting min-width and min-height to 44px on the button element, boundingBox returns width 44 and height 44 and the assertion passes.
K-019521.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and no line says 'Expected >= 44 Received 24'.
traps: Padding on the inner icon does not always grow the tap area. Set min-width and min-height on the button element itself.
Measure the button, not the SVG inside it, because the button is the real tap target.

steps.do: In tests/toast.stack.spec.ts, trigger three toasts in a row at viewport width 375.
Run the stacking test on the mobile-375 project.
In the same spec, assert the vertical gap between each pair of [data-testid=toast] boxes is at least 8px and the count is exactly 3.

K-019522.example: Three toasts render at tops 16, 90, and 164 with heights 66px each, so the gaps are 8px and 8px. The assertion for count 3 and gap at least 8 passes.
K-019522.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and the failure message would read 'Expected >= 8 Received 4' if gaps were too small.
traps: Small models often compare toast tops but forget heights. Compute the gap as next.y minus (prev.y plus prev.height).
Toasts may animate in. Wait for the count to reach 3 with expect.poll before reading boundingBox.

steps.do: In src/components/Toaster.test.tsx, mock window.matchMedia so that the query '(max-width: 640px)' returns matches true.
Render Toaster and assert the root element has the class toaster--bottom.
Run only the test named switches to bottom layout with Vitest.
steps.cmd: npx vitest run src/components/Toaster.test.tsx -t 'switches to bottom layout'

K-019523.example: With matchMedia mocked to match at max-width 640px, Toaster renders with class toaster--bottom. A second test with matches false asserts the class toaster--top-right instead.
K-019523.check: Output shows 'Tests 1 passed' and the earlier desktop case also passes when run without -t.
traps: Small models often forget to restore window.matchMedia after each test. Reset it in afterEach so later tests do not inherit the mobile state.
jsdom does not apply CSS media queries. Test the React class or prop switch, not the computed style.

steps.do: Build the production bundle.
Create the reports directory.
Start Vite preview on port 4173 in its own terminal and leave it running.
In a second terminal, confirm the preview server answers on the toast URL.
Run Lighthouse in mobile form factor on the page and save JSON to reports/lh-toast.json.
Read the Cumulative Layout Shift numeric value from the report.

K-019524.example: The toast mounts 400ms after load into a fixed-position container. The report shows numericValue 0.02, which is under the 0.1 limit.
K-019524.check: The jq command prints a number under 0.1, for example 0.02, and the Lighthouse run exits without an error line.
traps: Small models often read the performance score instead of the CLS audit. Check cumulative-layout-shift specifically and compare to 0.1.
Insert the toast into a fixed or absolute container. Inserting it into normal flow above content shifts the page and raises CLS.

steps.do: Confirm the list component file exists in the app.
Build the app for production.
Run the Playwright test that counts row elements in the DOM with 1000 items loaded.
Check the logged rowCount is 60 or fewer for 1000 items.

K-019525.example: ProductList renders 1000 products through a window of 40 visible rows, so the test expects at most 60 li elements with data-row set. The spec logs rowCount: 40 and passes.
K-019525.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the log shows rowCount: 40 or lower.
traps: Counting only visible rows misses nodes that stay mounted off-screen.
Testing with 20 items proves nothing about a 1000-item list.
Hiding rows with the hidden class keeps them in the DOM, so the count does not drop.

steps.do: Build the app for production.
In a second terminal, serve the built app on port 4173.
Run Lighthouse on the products route with only the performance category.
Read the performance score from the JSON report.
Fail the change if the score is below 0.90.

K-019526.example: After lazy-loading thumbnails, the products list scores 0.93, which passes the 0.90 gate. The change is blocked if the jq output is 0.87.
K-019526.check: jq prints a number of 0.90 or higher, for example 0.93.
traps: Running Lighthouse against the Vite dev server gives scores that do not reflect production.
Scoring the home route instead of the products route tests the wrong page.
Lighthouse reports scores from 0 to 1, so 90 is never the right threshold value.

steps.do: Compile Tailwind with minification from the input file.
Measure the compiled file size in bytes.
Confirm the divide-y utility made it into the compiled output.
Check the file size is under 30000 bytes.

K-019527.example: After adding divide-y and space-y-2 to the product list, wc reports 18432 bytes. The rg count of 1 shows the utility is present in the single minified line.
K-019527.check: wc prints a byte count under 30000 and rg prints 1 because minified CSS is one line.
traps: Skipping the minify flag inflates the size and makes the check meaningless.
Measuring the source input.css instead of the compiled output file.
Reading the rg count as occurrences, since minified CSS puts everything on one line.

steps.do: Confirm the arbitrary content-visibility class is applied in the list file.
Run the Playwright test that scrolls 1000 rows and records layout shift.
Run Lighthouse on the products route and save the JSON report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.
Check the cumulative layout shift value is 0.1 or lower.

K-019528.example: Each li uses the arbitrary classes that set content-visibility to auto and contain-intrinsic-size to auto 64px, so off-screen rows reserve height. The report then shows a cumulative layout shift of 0.02.
K-019528.check: The Playwright run prints '1 passed' and jq prints a number of 0.1 or lower.
traps: Omitting contain-intrinsic-size makes the scrollbar jump, which raises layout shift.
Applying content-visibility to the whole list container instead of each item hides the list.
Skipping the scroll step means the test never reaches the rows that cause the shift.

steps.do: Count the lazy-loading attributes in the list component.
Build the app for production.
Run the Playwright test that counts image requests before any scrolling.
Check the logged image request count is 6 before scrolling.

K-019529.example: The first six product thumbnails load eagerly and the remaining 194 use loading set to lazy, so the test expects exactly 6 requests before scroll. The spec logs requested images: 6 and passes.
K-019529.check: The spec prints requested images: 6 and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Setting lazy loading on the first visible rows delays the largest contentful paint image.
Counting img tags in the HTML is not the same as counting real network requests.
Images inside display none containers can behave differently, so test the rendered layout.

steps.do: Confirm the scroll handler is throttled with requestAnimationFrame.
Run the Playwright scroll benchmark over 1000 rows.
Read the timing results the test wrote to disk.
Check the median handler time is 8ms or lower.
Check the longest frame during a 3 second scroll is 16ms or lower.

K-019530.example: A 3 second scroll over 1000 rows records a median handler time of 4.2ms and a longest frame of 14ms, inside the 8ms and 16ms budgets. The test fails if the median reaches 9ms.
K-019530.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the JSON shows medianMs of 8 or lower and maxFrameMs of 16 or lower.
traps: Benchmarking only on a fast desktop hides slowdowns that appear on mobile CPUs.
Reporting an average instead of the longest frame hides jank spikes.
Using setInterval for scroll state instead of rAF throttling causes extra work per frame.

steps.do: List the color tokens already defined in the global stylesheet.
Check whether any reduced motion rules already exist.
Plan text links to reach at least 4.5:1 contrast against their background, and nav icons and borders to reach at least 3:1.
Plan every nav link and button to have a minimum height and width of 44px, and record the planned values in a table.

K-019531.example: The plan lists the link color as #1a4fb3 on a white background, which needs a ratio of at least 4.5:1, and sets nav links to min-height 44px. The reduced motion check finds no matches, so the plan adds one media query for the nav transition.
K-019531.check: The plan table has one row per text and background pair with a ratio of at least 4.5:1, and every nav link row shows 44px or more.
traps: Small models often pick brand colors without checking the contrast ratio against the actual background.
A 24px target can pass the minimum but is harder to tap, so the plan should use 44px.
Contrast checks are verified later with npx axe, so do not claim them done at the planning stage.

steps.do: Find where the EmptyState widget is defined in the source tree.
Run the render budget test that times 1000 draws into a TestBackend.
Run the text visibility test that checks the placeholder string is in the buffer.
Run the whole crate test suite to catch regressions.

K-019532.example: EmptyState draws 'No items yet' into an 80x24 TestBackend. The budget test asserts that 1000 draws finish in under 200ms, which is an average of 0.2ms per frame.
K-019532.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed' and the budget test shows no timeout panic.
traps: TestBackend measures draw cost, not real terminal flush cost, so do not claim the 16ms frame budget from it alone.
A debug build can be about 10 times slower than release, so compare numbers only within the same profile.
Do not widen the 200ms threshold to make a failing test pass.

steps.do: Find the EmptyState class and where the app mounts it.
Run the empty state test file to confirm the baseline passes.
Run the mount timing test that enforces the 50ms limit.
Run the pilot test that confirms the placeholder Static with id empty-hint is visible.

K-019533.example: A pilot run_test() mounts the app with zero rows and records the time from start to first render. The test asserts that mount completes in under 50ms and that the Static with id empty-hint is visible.
K-019533.check: pytest prints '2 passed' with no failures, and a mount over 50ms fails with an AssertionError that shows the measured milliseconds.
traps: Textual's run_test runs headless, so it does not measure real terminal output speed.
Calling query_one before mount finishes raises an error, so await the mount first.
Do not raise the 50ms limit to force a pass.

steps.do: Find the draw call site in the event loop.
Run the test that counts frames across 10 idle ticks with no data.
Run the test that confirms one data change adds exactly one extra draw.
Run clippy to catch unused redraw flags.

K-019534.example: With no data, 10 idle ticks must produce 1 draw in total, the initial frame. Adding one item must bring the total to exactly 2 draws.
K-019534.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok' for both tests, and the draw counter reads 1 after the idle ticks.
traps: Ratatui redraws the full frame on each terminal.draw call, so count calls rather than visible changes.
A counter placed in the wrong spot also counts resize events.
Do not delete the test to get a green result.

steps.do: Locate the reactive attribute that controls whether the empty state shows.
Run the pilot test that loads one record and checks the hint is removed.
Run the latency test that enforces the 16ms limit after pilot.pause.
Run the full Textual empty state test file.

K-019535.example: Posting a DataLoaded message with one row removes the EmptyState widget, and the test asserts removal within 16ms of pilot.pause. The full file finishes in under 2 seconds.
K-019535.check: pytest prints '3 passed' with no NoMatches error.
traps: Await pilot.pause before asserting, or the removal may not have been processed yet.
Setting display to False leaves the widget in the tree, so count the children instead.
Do not raise the 16ms limit to get a pass.

steps.do: Check which SvelteKit store API the project uses, the newer $app/state or the older $app/stores.
Count the links the nav component renders, since each link needs an aria-current decision.
Plan to set aria-current to page on the active link only, and leave the attribute off the others.
Plan a visible style for the active link, such as bold text or an underline, so the state is not shown by color alone.
Check the contrast of the active link text against its background, which must be at least 4.5:1.

K-019536.example: With $app/state, the plan uses the expression aria-current={page.url.pathname === link.href ? 'page' : undefined} on each anchor, and the count of href attributes in Nav.svelte is 5. The active link gets font-weight 700 and an underline, and the axe run reports 0 color-contrast violations.
K-019536.check: The plan names exactly one aria-current expression, grep -c 'href=' prints the planned link count such as 5, and npx @axe-core/cli reports 0 color-contrast violations at 4.5:1.
traps: Small models often write aria-current true instead of page, which is less specific.
Do not use a color change as the only signal for the active link.
Do not mix $app/state and $app/stores in one plan.

steps.do: Check whether the project already has a menu toggle that sets aria-expanded.
Check whether the project already handles the Escape key in components.
Check whether the project already sets a 44px minimum touch target size.
Plan a button with aria-expanded bound to a $state boolean and aria-controls pointing to the id of the menu list.
Plan an onkeydown handler that closes the menu on Escape and moves focus back to the button.

K-019537.example: The plan uses let open = $state(false), a button with aria-expanded={open} and aria-controls='site-menu', and a ul with id='site-menu' that uses the hidden attribute when open is false. The button has min-height 44px. Escape sets open to false and calls the button focus method.
K-019537.check: rg -n 'aria-controls' src prints 1 line, rg -c 'site-menu' src/lib/components/Nav.svelte prints 2 (one aria-controls and one id), and the button min-height is 44px or more.
traps: Small models often use a div with a click handler instead of a button element, which breaks keyboard access.
The aria-controls value must match an existing id, or assistive technology cannot link the button to the menu.
